request: Wire the Stitch (Google Labs AI UI design tool) MCP server into Claude Code; document the Stitch -> ui/ kit translation convention; apply it to build one screen (Login + Menu navigation) the user designed in Stitch, mirroring the charges gold-standard slice.

decisions.decision: The Stitch screen to translate is the Login screen plus the Menu navigation (redesign-or-new TBD by the design at grill time; data + read paths pinned then).
MCP scope is the committed project .mcp.json (shared; token via ${STITCH_API_TOKEN} env expansion), NOT user-level ~/.claude/mcp_servers.json.

The grill-me pass (required by openspec/config.yaml) runs AFTER the Stitch MCP is connected (Claude Code restart + confirm Stitch tools), so the Login+Menu data model and read paths are grilled against the actual design.

DESIGN.md -> custom DaisyUI theme mapping is DEFERRED (not part of this change). Will be recorded in openspec/roadmaps/backlog.md when wanted; this change only translates one Stitch screen into a ui/-kit slice.

SUPersedes D2: the Stitch MCP connection is GLOBAL (user's global opencode/Claude Code MCP config, available to any project), NOT project-scoped. Rationale: Stitch is a general design tool, not this project's infrastructure. This repo keeps only the translation-convention doc (ai/htmx-conventions.md) and no Stitch config or secret. Also corrects the transport: Stitch is a REMOTE server at https://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp with an X-Goog-Api-Key header (env-indirected via {env:STITCH_API_KEY}), not the @google/stitch-mcp stdio wrapper D2 assumed.

Login is a VISUAL re-skin of the EXISTING Google login flow (login.templ already links /auth/google/login). Stitch's email+password inputs, the 'Sign In' primary button, and the 'OR' divider are DROPPED. The 'Continue with Google' button is kept, wired to /auth/google/login. No new auth module, no DB change, no Google OIDC password flow introduced.

Nav header (vehicle name + battery % + status dot) reads the LATEST vehicle snapshot via the EXISTING telemetry.Reader.LatestSnapshotsByAccount port (BatteryLevel) joined with account's vehicle name (account port). Status/label derived from snapshot FRESHNESS (CapturedAt within recent window => 'Connected'+green; else 'Asleep'/'Last seen'). No new read path, no new module, no DB object.

The Stitch nav's 'Wake Vehicle' button is DROPPED. It conflicts with AGENTS.md's Data Access Model ('users never trigger Tesla API calls on demand', exception is only listing vehicles at first connect). No button is rendered.

Stitch nav items 'Supercharger Stats' and 'Settings' are rendered as dead/placeholder links (route present or stub, page NOT built this change). Both recorded in openspec/roadmaps/backlog.md as future work (Supercharger Stats screen + Settings page).

Stitch nav items 'Dashboard' => /dashboard and 'Manual Records' => /charges are mapped to the EXISTING pages. Reasonable alternative existed (drop/relabel); user only confirmed the two placeholders in the multi-select, so taken as the obvious default to avoid a third grill round.

home.templ debug artifacts ('Visits this session' line + the 'Check database' htmx health-fragment demo) are REMOVED in this change. Rest of the landing (signed-in state, Connect Tesla link, Log out) untouched. No 'NO DB Change' text exists in any gateway .templ (confirmed by grep).

Stitch's inline <script> (parallax + focus-scale) and ALL inline JS are DROPPED (zero-JS convention). The Stitch background image references an external googleusercontent URL — replaced by an embedded local asset OR a CSS gradient per the no-external-CDN/embedded-asset rule. Exact treatment decided in design.md.
